title: Thrummed mittens
subtitle: Aran-weight mittens insulated with raw fleece thrums worked into the knitting.
excerpt: Full mittens in Aran-weight yarn with raw fleece thrums inserted every third stitch on the inner face. The thrums felt slightly when worn, creating a naturally warm lining. Gusseted thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Thrummed mittens are a traditional technique from Newfoundland, Canada, and parallel traditions exist across Scandinavia and the British Isles. The technique is documented in Katharine Annis and M.K. Eckman, Thrummed Knitting (multiple editions from 1992), in the Newfoundland and Labrador Folk Arts Society publications, and cross-referenced in regional craft surveys.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts x 24 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4.5 mm needles. The thrum rows pull in slightly; the overall gauge should be checked on the plain rounds.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small length of raw or lightly-prepared fleece, about 10 to 15 cm long, folded in half and knitted into a stitch so that the fleece tails fall to the inside of the fabric. When worn, body heat causes the fleece to mat gently, creating a warm insulating lining. The word 'thrum' originally referred to the unwoven fringe end of a warp thread on a loom.

A wedge of extra stitches added gradually to build the thumb opening. Increases run along both sides of a marker to match the natural widening of the hand at the base of the thumb. The gusset stitches are placed on hold while the hand is finished, then worked for the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens in Aran-weight yarn with raw fleece
thrums
inserted every few stitches on the inner face.
Gusseted thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

Each thrum is a 12 cm length of raw fleece folded in half and knitted in by looping the fold around the working needle before drawing the stitch through. The tails hang to the inside of the tube and felt into a warm, soft layer after a few wearings. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 140 g of Aran yarn and 50 g of raw fleece (any wool breed, uncarded or lightly carded). Wash the fleece before thrumming to remove lanolin.
What you need

items.name: Main yarn
items.qty: 140 g (about 240 m / 265 yards) of Aran-weight wool

items.name: Raw fleece
items.qty: 50 g of washed raw or lightly-carded fleece. Any soft wool breed; avoid coarse fleece.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4.5 mm (UK 7 / US 7) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 2 to flank the thumb gusset

items.name: Scrap yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm to hold gusset stitches

content.text: Preparing thrums

Pull the fleece into strips roughly 1 cm wide. Tear into lengths of 12 cm. Prepare about 80 thrums per mitten before you start. The length is not critical; 10 to 14 cm all work. Thrums prepared in advance keep a rhythm when knitting.
Thrum stitch

attrs.heading: How to work a thrum stitch

items.name: Step 1
items.qty: Fold a thrum in half. Lay the folded loop around the right needle, folded end pointing away from you.

items.name: Step 2
items.qty: Insert the right needle into the next stitch as if to knit. Draw through the loop of the thrum, bringing it through the stitch alongside the working yarn.

items.name: Step 3
items.qty: The two tails of the thrum hang to the inside. On the next round, the thrum stitch is knitted normally, catching the tails firmly.

content.text: Thrum placement

attrs.heading: 2-round thrum repeat. Plain rounds alternate with thrum rounds.

items.name: Round A (thrum)
items.qty: *k2, T1*; repeat. T1 = work 1 thrum stitch.

content.text: Gauge
18 stitches and 24 rounds to 10 cm in plain stocking stitch on 4.5 mm needles. The thrum rounds pull in slightly; check gauge on a plain round.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and rib cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 14 (16, 16) rounds of 1x1 rib. Thrumming does not start until the hand; the rib cuff is worked plain.
Thumb gusset

Set up gusset: knit to last 3 stitches of the palm, PM, k1, PM, knit to end. Continue in plain stocking stitch. Gusset increase round: knit to marker, SM, M1L, knit to next marker, M1R, SM, knit to end. Knit 2 plain rounds. Repeat until the gusset holds 9 (11, 11) stitches. Thread gusset stitches onto scrap yarn. Cast on 1 stitch over the gap.
Hand with thrums
Begin the 2-round thrum repeat across the full hand: alternate one thrum round and one plain round. Continue for 28 (30, 32) rounds.
Top shaping

Work the top in plain stocking stitch (no thrums on the final rounds). Place a midpoint marker. Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Thumb
Return 9 (11, 11) held gusset stitches to needles. Pick up 1 stitch from the gap. Work 4 rounds of the thrum repeat followed by 4 (6, 6) plain rounds. Bind off.
Common faults

Thrums sit on the outside rather than the inside: the thrum was looped the wrong way. The fold of the thrum must pass through the stitch to the inside. Check that the tails hang on the purl side of the fabric.

Thrums come loose after a few wearings: the tails are too short or too fine. Use thrums at least 10 cm long. Short tails will not mat sufficiently. The mitts can be put in the washing machine on a low wool cycle after the first wearing to help the thrums felt in.
Finishing
Weave in all yarn tails on the wrong side. Trim any thrum tails longer than 6 cm so they do not bunch. The first wearing will begin the felting process.
Care
Hand wash in cool water or gentle machine wash on a wool cycle. Do not tumble dry. The thrums will felt gradually with wear and washing, increasing warmth over time. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
Thrumming can be applied to any plain mitten pattern at Aran gauge. The technique also works for boot insoles and slippers, where the thrummed fabric felts into a firm inner lining.
